An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic events into three segments, based on energy: an extremely energetic group above 43 EeV, a very energetic group between 11-43 EeV, and a more energetic group between 8-11 EeV. We discovered a substantial anisotropy signal in the most energetic group above 11 EeV, with an amplitude of $ (1.5\pm0.8_{\rm stat}\pm0.7_{\rm syst})^{\circ}$ and a quadrupolar component in the most energetic group above 8 EeV, with an amplitude of $ (2.5\pm1.7_{\rm stat}\pm1.4_{\rm syst})^{\circ}$. No significant anisotropy was found in the most energetic group above 11 EeV or the most energetic group above 43 EeV. The anisotropy signal in the most energetic group between 11-43 EeV, with an amplitude of $ (1.7\pm1.0_{\rm stat}\pm0.8_{\rm syst})^{\circ

The ATLAS detector at the LHC studied the production of charged particles in lead-lead collisions at 2.76 TeV and 5.02 TeV.  After adjusting for detector efficiency and background, a comparison was made between the nuclear modification factor and transverse charge particle production at various energies.  It was found that the nuclear modification factor increases with energy from 54 GeV to 130 GeV, but then decreases above 250 GeV.  Additionally, the ratio of charged particles to pions also increases with energy from 54 GeV to 1.9 TeV.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, characterized by specific commutation relations that define the structure constants of a Lie algebra. By transforming the coordinates into linear differential operators in a commuting momentum space, we can reformulate this issue into an ordinary quantum problem. These operators, representing the coordinates $\hat x_a$, have a form $-i\hat D_a = -iE_{ab}(p)\partial /\partial p_b$, where $E_{ab}$ can be expressed as an infinite series over the deformation parameter $\theta$. The deformed Hamiltonian $\hat H$ describes the motion on corresponding group manifolds with sizes proportional to $\theta^{-1}$, whose metrics also appear in certain infinite series of $\theta$. The matrices $E_{ab}$ can be represented in simple forms for certain algebras like $su(2)$ and $u(N)$. Additionally, our study has been extended to nonabelian Poisson brackets, the harmonic oscillator, and the massless Dirac fermion in $[X_a,X_b]=\theta_{ab}$ noncommutative spaces.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we compared the results of training models using both a federated approach and a centralized approach. Our findings indicate that federated learning can produce models with similar accuracy to those trained with centralized data, while avoiding the need to collect extensive training datasets at a single location. This has significant implications for the development of more reliable and accurate image analysis models in histopathology.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 72Gbit/s using the on-off keying technique, over a distance of 18.8km in a South China Sea submarine cable that lacks dispersion compensation.  Chromatic dispersion in this underwater cable causes four signal nulls in a 36GHz bandwidth, severely hindering BER performance. To address this issue, a decision feedback equalizer was initially applied with satisfactory results, however its effectiveness was impeded due to the occurrence of burst errors resulting from unpredictable marine conditions. To mitigate this issue, a weighted DFE method was developed but proved insufficient as it was unable to fully compensate for the spectral distortions due to the limited scope of its feedback symbols. To address these limitations, the introduction of maximum likelihood sequence estimation after WDFE proved capable of both rectifying the spectral distortions and providing optimal detection, ultimately yielding a maximum 2.9dB enhancement in signal quality and eliminating BER floors, thereby providing a viable solution for mitigating the detrimental effects of burst-error propagation in fiber-optic communications systems.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which typically demands significant experimentation. We've developed a technique to automate the dilation optimization process by casting it as a weight-pruning operation along the time axis. Our method learns dilation factors concurrently with weights during training and achieves notable gains in model compactness and inference efficiency without compromising accuracy. It produces a range of highly optimal TCN variants from a single starting model, surpassing the performance of custom-designed networks in both efficiency and accuracy.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude are evident across different centralities and become more pronounced in more central collisions and in collisions where the momentum of the particles is higher than 2 GeV/c. These findings, which have been compared to theoretical models such as iEBE-VISHNU, MUSIC, and AMPT, shed new light on the complex and not well understood initial conditions of these collisions. Furthermore, they highlight unique sensitivities to two crucial factors: the viscosity of quark--gluon plasma and the characteristics of the collisions' initial state. Given that these fluctuations tend to increase with the momentum of the particles, there is a need for re-examining existing theoretical models to gain a more precise and unbiased understanding of quark--gluon plasma's properties.

The existing correspondence theory for Sahlqvist logician friends is now combined with algebraic semantics, resulting in a unified framework that incorporates both correspondence and coalgebraic approaches. This unified framework specifically builds upon the Sahlqvist correspondence theorem to extend the reach of bisimulation tractability to arbitrary monotone modal logics. A new, hybrid proof scheme has been developed to capture the corresponding algebraic semantics proofs, and this scheme already embodies the principles of the correspondence theory. Furthermore, this unified approach already subsumes and generalizes both the correspondence theory and the earlier results on modal logic with an order, as seen in the context of algebraic semantics.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explore theories for handling instances that breach certain dependencies, with no preconditions on the presence of missing values. We establish a framework where each data entry can be assigned a truth status of true, false, inconsistent, or undetermined. To facilitate this framework, we develop data quality indicators that gauge data completeness, accuracy, and consistency. To further this research, we invite fellow theorists to contribute their ideas on how to extend and refine these concepts.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within such data sets. Furthermore, we have developed an estimation framework utilizing maximum score equity that enables parameter calculations for our TV-PARX model. Simulation results demonstrate the efficacy and reliability of this approach. To illustrate its practical applications, we conduct a real-world forecasting exercise utilizing daily COVID-19 case counts across 139 Italian provinces.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and between-them distances, using a combination of
rotation and translation transformations, meeting certain SE(3) equivariance conditions.
We demonstrate that this representation, operating within defined symmetry constraints,
enables the removal of object ambiguities and facilitates its unique identification.
We further establish that certain Neural Network architectures, applying NDFs and adhering
to those constraints, automatically produce outputs indicative of object invariants, such
as shapes and categories, without needing additional classification layers.
Through experiments on 3D object manipulation tasks, we show that Neural Descriptor
Fields achieve state-of-the-art performance on both scene parsing and object recognition
tasks, obtained without any additional layers or specialized loss functions.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet precision demands for the Higgs boson and other research areas while maintaining an adaptable sensitivity to diverse potential discoveries. The SiD's robust silicon vertex and tracking system, complemented by its high central magnetic field, ensures precise momentum measurement. The detector's finely granulated calorimeter system, designed for particle flow analysis, delivers accurate energy resolution across a wide energy range. Given the approaching construction timeline for the ILC, the time has come to reassess the design choices made during the design phase and incorporate the recent breakthroughs in technology into the review process. This review will discuss R&D prospects and the associated scientific implications for potential upgrades or revisions to the design during the pre-approval phase.

This study presents the first detailed analysis of seven red giant members of the distant globular cluster Tononzintla 2. The abundance of elements was determined for five cluster members, using the spectrum of a nitrogen-enriched hot blue straggler star excluded from this sample. The abundance of elements in the other six red giant members of the cluster ranges from -0.64 to -0.05 in [Fe/H], with a standard deviation of 0.34, indicating a metal content similar to other southern hemisphere globular clusters with similar metallic content. The abundance of elements was also determined for abundance patterns of C, N, O, Na, Mg, Al, and Ca, showing little variation in elements except for nitrogen, with values ranging from -0.14 to 0.71 in [N/Fe], with a standard deviation of 0.54, indicating a wide range of nitrogen enrichment likely resulting from multiple generations of stars with different nitrogen content, with no evidence of anti-anti-correlation found in this cluster. The study also determined an oxygen content of [O/Fe] = 0.06, with an uncertainty of 0.17, indicating an oxygen over-metallic enrichment similar to other southern hemisphere globular clusters with similar metallic content, with no variation in oxygen content found among the seven red giant members of the cluster. The study also determined an [Al/Fe] abundance of 0.38, with an uncertainty of 0.17

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing an impressive compilation of research and offering a diverse range of opportunities for statistical exploration in the field of theorem proving. Despite the numerous contributions made so far, the ever-expanding nature of the archive still poses certain challenges: locating specific content has become increasingly difficult, making it essential to prioritize reuse and clarity of comprehension. This thesis proposal outlines my research objectives, which focus on these concerns, as follows: firstly, I aim to devise an evaluation method measuring the discoverability of the archive by assessing the findability of its contents; secondly, I intend to develop a visualization tool to present the structure and content of the archive, thereby enhancing the comprehension of its contents.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have previously found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.68 for $N=2, 4$ although these earlier results have a larger systematic uncertainty.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can converge to a point that represents a minimum or a local optimum. To address this concern, we have developed an explicit characterization of the local convexity properties for the optimization landscape associated with a specific non-convex functional regularization method, specifically Group-Lasso. This characterization applies to both vector and matrix contexts. Our main contribution involves an innovative application of an established inequality from convex analysis. This allows us to utilize it in a way that has not been previously done to obtain a local convexity property. This property is crucial for ensuring the convergence of an established optimization algorithm under certain conditions. We have also discovered that a specific quantity, which we refer to as the'sparsity envelope', serves as a local convexity 'barrier' that defines the boundaries of local convex regions within the model. This quantity provides a measure of the minimum local convexity of the model and is determined by the norms of specific vectors that are directly related to the model.

Modern science and technology classify a metasurface by its intricate design, unknown chiral properties, and mysterious response to electromagnetic signals. Despite numerous studies on metasurfaces, their mysterious nature remains unbroken. This report challenges this perception, asserting that a metasurface's behavior can be understood through its local electromagnetic characteristics at a specific point. By analyzing the time-averaged Poynting vector and applying mathematical transformations, we demonstrate that any metasurface can be represented as a combination of normal incident waves with predetermined amplitudes and phases. This report provides a theoretical framework for comprehending metasurfaces and provides a practical method for predicting a metasurface's behavior based on its local properties. This approach is exemplified through numerical simulations and measurements of reflection coefficients from various metasurfaces, offering a straightforward path to designing customized metasurfaces.

This research builds upon previous findings by Ruiz and Sanchez-Valentin regarding smooth vector fields in the vicinity of nondegenerate singular points, with the added assumption that a full complement of nearby first integrals exists. We expand this theorem by removing the nondegeneracy assumption for the singular point, while still concluding that a nearby linearized homoclinic transition is genetically equivalent to one localized at the original singular point.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which can learn simplified potential functions
that accurately capture the intricate instantaneous relationships among electrons
within complex atomic systems. Trained in an unsupervised manner with constrained
data derived from Full Configuration Interaction one-electron density functions, the
eCPNN model effectively predicts total atomic energies with remarkable precision.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed a Giant Arc, which lies at a redshift of approximately 0.8. Spanning nearly 1 billion light-years, this feature exhibits remarkable symmetry when viewed from space. It was discovered through a novel approach using intervening magnesium-absorbing systems in the light from background quasars. Our analysis leverages a range of techniques: hierarchical clustering, a statistical test, and power spectrum analysis - each method providing unique insights, which together suggest the presence of a massive structure at around 4.5 to 4.8 sigma confidence levels. We employed multiple statistical tests to mitigate any biases that could influence our findings, which suggest that the arc-like feature is an overdensity with a density ratio of about 1.3, with a 30% margin of error. The Giant Arc represents one of the largest and most intriguing examples of a massive cosmic structure that could challenge the cosmological principle underpinning our current understanding of the universe. It may be an early stage in the formation of a massive structure like the Sloan Great Wall or the Hercules-Corona Cloud, which eventually gave rise to massive clusters of galaxies.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may offer precise measurements of aerosol optical depth, a significant challenge lies in achieving the necessary accuracy. A notable source of inaccuracy stems from systematic errors present in in-flight measurements of the TESS spacecraft. These errors, stemming from variations in the telescope's temperature and field, were initially thought to be a major obstacle. Nevertheless, they were overcome through improvements to the data processing system. Nevertheless, they were still too great to be overcome even with the significant enhancements made to the observation protocol. As such, a new data processing system was developed, incorporating a model that accounts for temperature-driven distortions in the telescope's field. This new system, built utilizing a sophisticated Gaussian model, was capable of mitigating the inaccuracies associated with the telescope itself. As such, it is now feasible to achieve accurate measurements of aerosol optical depth using in-flight measurements of the TESS spacecraft.

Recently, estimating a 3D object's pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest. Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNNs derive object features and regional features, followed by PTransformNetworks calculating pose parameters. The CNNS object-recognition module's performance largely depends on its training dataset. Overfitting may occur when training with relatively small datasets, especially when pose parameters are trained with supervised learning. To address this challenge, we present a new loss function called the Disentanglement Loss Function (DLF) that encourages the decoupling of object features from pose parameters, thereby regularizing Deep Neural Networks. By applying DLF to the intermediate feature module, we achieve significant performance improvements. Our experiments demonstrate that DLF leads to substantial gains in accuracy and reduces overfitting when employing publicly available datasets, resulting in superior results when compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, due to their ability to model and track discontinuity formation within materials. Bond-based Peridynamics, despite its modeling restrictions, has become a widely-used approach in numerical simulations because of its ease of implementation and intuitive connection to real-world physics. This paper delves into the aspects of bond-based peridynamic models, providing a thorough examination of the theory and its numerical representations. Various bond-based PD integral kernels have been presented along with their distinguishing characteristics, leading to discussions on their implications and common traits. A closer examination was conducted on the role of non-locality in determining motion, the interplay between kernel structure and material non-penetration, as well as the influence of PD kernel non-linearity on predicting fracture development. Finally, an exploration is initiated on adapting BB-PD to model fluids within the context of fading memory materials, suggesting directions for enhanced understanding of fluid dynamics within the peridynamic framework.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
hidden variables in Chandrasekaran (2012) and can jointly estimate multiple
inverse covariance matrices, as shown in Danaher (2013) and Tomasi (2018). The
GGLasso package supports the resolution of diverse formulations and notable
subcases like Graphical Lasso with latent variables, Group, and Fused Graphical Lasso.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and assessed, focusing on deterministic impulses, drifts, and Brownian motions. By utilizing the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion, recent studies found that the methods' accuracy could be evaluated in terms of the impact of the step size on configurational averaging. Results showed that for harmonic oscillators, some methods yield precise configurational averages, potentially leading to better performance in biomolecular simulations, especially in cases where bond stretches play a crucial roles. Furthermore, research found that an optimal method could be identified that offers high precision in configurational averaging at no additional computational cost, when compared to existing techniques. Through scalable implementations, this work explored the benefits of the optimal method in large molecular systems. Findings indicated that even minor improvements to common methods, such as the velocity Verlet and Langevin integrators, could result in substantial reductions in thermal fluctuations and drift errors, significantly enhancing the precision of configurational averages in biomolecular simulations.

Numerical relativity simulations allow us to study how binary black hole mergers interact with their surroundings. However, these simulations start only shortly before the merger and require predetermined initial conditions to proceed. Therefore, a significant task involves identifying the appropriate configuration for the binary system and its environment at this point in the process. In our research, we've been investigating the behavior of dark matter in the vicinity of black hole binaries of equal mass, discovering a consistent, long-lasting profile that emerges over several orbits. Conversely, systems with greater dark matter mass see overdensities scattered due to the binary's motion. When we induce a binary black hole merger in systems with equal mass, the dark matter's response is characterized by the release of scalar waves with specific frequencies tied to the binary's motion. However, if we allow the binary to separate into two distinct objects, the dark matter's behavior changes, with overdensities forming around each object. Systems with greater dark matter mass exhibit more pronounced overdensities in both scenarios. Our findings provide a foundation for improving approximate models used in future studies.

This study examines the exponential stability of a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The outer points where these branches meet are fixed while rotating. The results show that the asymptotic spectrum's structure and its eigenmodes' characteristics provide a complete analysis of the system's exponential stability. Specifically, if the rotational fixation at the junction is sufficiently strong, the system achieves exponential stability, and its asymptotic spectrum consists of three isolated clusters each displaying polynomial, exponential, and Hermite-type decay. Conversely, if the rotational fixation at the junction is not sufficiently strong, the system's stability is only polynomial and its asymptotic spectrum consists of two clusters with polynomial and Hermite-type decay, and one cluster with distinct real part values.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses composed of PMMA to increase the detection area of sensitive devices and improve resolution but discovered these lenses introduced image distortion. This problem was investigated and a new lens material called Stycast 1090SI was proposed as an alternative. The acoustic properties of this novel material were examined alongside PMMA to determine its feasibility. Computational simulations and practical tests using two different materials, PMMA and Stycast 1090SI, showed both materials significantly enhance the detection capabilities of sensitive devices. Notably, the Stycast lens exhibited lower levels of distortion compared to the PMMA lens, which could have implications for photoacoustic tomography technology.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, with an innovative new component that simultaneously demosaicks and deblurs them in an interpretable way. To train this model, we utilize real-world camera data transformed into raw images through a realistic process, mimicking real-world camera functions. By doing so, we demonstrate the advantages of our single-stage model over traditional approaches combining demosaicking and deblurring modules, according to objective performance metrics. Additionally, our method is capable of removing a camera's intrinsic blurring effect, which effectively enables deblurring of sharp images.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of the 'cdt' package, which executes a comprehensive causal discovery process to identify the causal interactions and the causal network structure among the variables, drawing from established methodologies including those from 'Bnlearn' and 'Pcalg', in addition to pairwise algorithms like ANM. The framework is available on GitHub under the terms of the permissive MIT License.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules describing when and how the sphere's surface breaks through the water's surface have been developed through the analysis of slow-speed impacts, revealing a more complex splash dome at intermediate speeds. In contrast, faster-speed impacts see the sphere's surface seal regime give way to a different, "reentrant" break-up pattern. Computer simulations, such as smooth particle hydrodynamics (SPH), are used to explore the underlying dynamics of the surface seal regime, with findings showing its key characteristics to be heavily influenced by the sphere's initial velocity, its interaction with the water's surface, and the resulting "splash wave" it generates.

A well-known hypothesis posits that at the fundamental level, effective field theories lacking global symmetries are gauge theories. We investigate the converse idea, assuming that fundamental $\theta$-terms are universal, to explore the implications for QCD. Specifically, we analyze the scenario where $\frac{\alpha_s}{4\pi}\theta$ is a global symmetry-breaking term within the context of the holographic Yang-Mills theory for QCD. We examine the connection between the $\theta$-term and axion density by considering both the symmetry-breaking $\theta$-term and an additional $\theta$-term generated by boundary cosmological constant within the holographic setup. We then investigate the axion problem by describing the behavior of the $\theta$-term as a function of temperature and density in both cases. We also explore the axion overabundance problem by relating the generated $\theta$-term to the vacuum expectation value of the axion field within the holographic setup. We investigate both the symmetry-breaking $\theta$-term and the $\theta$-term generated by boundary cosmological constant. We examine the former in the context of the $\mathrm{SU}(2|\mathrm{N})/\mathrm{SU}(2|\mathrm{N-1})$ holographic Yang-Mills theory and the latter in the context of the $\mathrm{SU}(N|\mathrm{M})/\mathrm{SU}(N|\mathrm{M-1})$ holographic

Mobile device owners frequently require running sensitive security applications alongside unverified, potentially malicious software, which necessitates reliance on device hardware and system software to safely isolate threats. 

This often misplaced trust is the foundation on which our objective is built – namely to minimize the reliance on device hardware and software components for users to withstand cyber threats. 

We introduce an innovative multi-domain hardware setup consisting of isolated sections, where programs are partitioned statically to prevent malicious interaction. 

A few key hardware components with proven security functionality are integrated to grant secure temporary access to processing resources and external input/output interfaces simultaneously.

To manage these hardware components, we develop a novel memory-safe operating system based on Rust, ensuring that device hardware and software cannot bypass security protocols.

As proof of concept, we design and construct a multi-domain hardware setup and an accompanying operating system for smartphones, leveraging established security hardware like Trusted Execution Environments.

Our results demonstrate that this approach can prevent nearly all types of attack vectors, significantly enhancing user security without needing substantial hardware upgrades.

We investigated the challenges of robust reinforcement learning in scenarios where an adaptive adversary intentionally manipulates rewards and transition probabilities. The adversary's influence is confined to no more than an $\epsilon$ fraction of all training episodes. Notably, this attack model surpasses previously considered methods. We established a key finding that no reinforcement learning algorithm can discover an optimal policy better than $O(\epsilon)$ under these circumstances. Interestingly, we discovered that the natural policy gradient method can be robust when the corruption is bounded and is capable of finding an $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$-optimal policy. We developed a filter-based algorithm that can achieve an $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$-optimal policy and established the efficacy of linear least-squares algorithms under mild assumptions. Moreover, we explored the feasibility of robust reinforcement learning in settings with adversarial target actions and action noise. Our findings demonstrate the possibility of finding a near-optimal policy in challenging environments through the utilization of multiple episodes and episode rewinding.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, holds the key to overcoming decoherence in quantum systems. In this work, researchers used ultrafast optical techniques to investigate multi-phonon correlations in a variety of systems, starting with dark excitons in semiconductor quantum dots. These dark states offer crucial insights due to their slow relaxation rates and weak coupling with phonons, allowing for the direct observation of multi-phonon states in a direct optical measurement. Ultrafast laser pulses were used to create dark excitons in a consistent manner, enabling the examination of correlation between phonons and exciton states. By analyzing the spectra of emitted light, containing information on phonon sequences, the researchers demonstrated the ability to distinguish between coherent phonon states and those that are incoherent. Furthermore, they measured the times between phonon emission and recombination, known as phonon lifetimes, for not only phonons surrounding the dark exciton but also for those associated with a vacuum state, reducing the estimated phonon lifetimes by half compared to previous studies, with a new estimate of 0.93 picoseconds. These findings provide a foundation for studying multi-phonon correlations in various quantum systems and may pave the way for improving quantum operations by taking phonons into consideration.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with two types of glide symmetries in perpendicular directions using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. This model contains horizontal and vertical hopping terms and reveals two distinct non-equivalent Dirac cones within the first Brillouin zone along a high-symmetry path. These cones can be modified through various perturbations of the Hamiltonian. These perturbations disrupt the lattice symmetries by applying differing onsite potentials at the lattice sites, which causes the Dirac cones to collapse into semi-Dirac cones and nodal lines along the high-symmetry paths. Next, we applied a dimerization to the hopping terms and observed the migration of the Dirac cones across the zone boundary or the folding of the cones into the zone boundary or the formation of a Klein bottle and cone in the half-filled case. Lastly, we simulated the lattice through a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model containing a Peierls on-site electron-phonon interaction and studied the balance between lattice distortion and band widening. This balance results in the migration of the Dirac cones or the formation of a semi-Dirac cone or the folding of the cone into the zone boundary or the formation of a Klein bottle and cone in the half-filled case.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with these phenomena under different conditions and find that they vary greatly, depending on the catalytic device used. Our analysis focuses particularly on the properties and the nonclassical character of SPCCSs produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers, and it is shown that the states generated in these two cases have distinct characteristics in terms of their structure and behavior in optical homodyning experiments.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 non-hydrogen atoms within a monomeric structure.

This paper presents a unified approach to addressing certain complex control problems. These control problems, which involve optimizing a system with both discrete and continuous components, can be formulated as multi-objective optimal control problems. Our method converts these problems into a single objective optimal control problem that can be solved using a relaxed dynamic programming technique. This enables us to find a suboptimal solution, which can be improved through the application of precise fixed points. Our approach ensures that the original constraints and requirements are met. To illustrate this method, we consider a system consisting of a first-order integrator and a discrete logic operator, and develop a control scheme to achieve a specific target by activating an on-off switch. This activation strategy is an optimal solution under certain conditions, but can result in suboptimal performance in other instances. We demonstrate the improvement that can be achieved through our proposed method.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other imaging techniques, medical histories, and endoscopic findings. Acquiring and combining these sources of information is time-consuming and sometimes produces inconclusive results. In this study, we investigate the potential for a more streamlined clinical approach where a limited review of CT scans is sufficient for labeling tumors. To support this approach, we developed a novel, lightweight labeling tool called AnnBTA that leverages human cognition to facilitate efficient and accurate tumor marking. This paper provides an in-depth analysis of the design considerations and algorithmic components of AnnBTA, along with an evaluation of its effectiveness in terms of user experience, system performance, and the quality of the annotated data obtained. Our results show that AnnBTA yields high-quality annotations with minimal data, outperforming a more complex state-of-the-art labeling method that requires more data.

The expense associated with drilling offshore wells is significant, as is the risk of delivering a well that fails to access planned reservoirs, thereby reducing potential hydrocarbon recoveries. Effectively managing these challenges is crucial for the economic viability of these projects. Advanced drilling technologies, particularly real-time data processing, have enhanced the feasibility of geosteering. This process involves continuously monitoring well progress in real-time using data from sensors located in the drill bit and along the wellbore, allowing adjustments to be made to steer the well towards optimal targets. Given the complexity of subsurface geology and the presence of uncertainties, implementing optimal control schemes requires a systematic approach to handle various factors such as different data schedules, varying levels of data loss, and uncertain well performance. This research introduces an innovative multi-objective Bayesian optimal control framework that can account for these uncertainties and data scheduling issues. The approach involves defining cost functions for controlling the well and scheduling data collection, followed by the application of evolutionary algorithms to identify optimal solutions. The effectiveness of this approach was demonstrated through simulations conducted on synthetic and actual well scenarios, showcasing its ability to provide a range of optimal solutions that can adapt to different levels of data loss.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique, extensively used to retrieve text-based information for further analysis. One type of NER, nested NER, focuses on recognizing entities within other entities. Most existing nested NER studies apply linear models, which do not adequately capture the hierarchical nature of nested entities. This work overcomes this limitation by modeling nested entities as an integrated whole and proposing a new parsing algorithm to accurately identify all entities at once. Empirical studies on standard datasets demonstrate the enhanced performance of our holistic model compared to linear-based and bi-directional models.

We extend the use of tropical methods to counting in arithmetic problems, such as the enumeration of lines touching a complex algebraic curve in the right way in an arithmetic setting. These counting problems often rely on geometric concepts like Grassmannians. In the case of curves, considering a specific type of touch, we can translate the problem into a question about points on a specific type of geometric structure called a matroid, which can be used to count touches using methods from tropical geometry. We show that for a certain type of curve called a plane curve, the count of touches, when adjusted for how many times they occur, is the same whether we're looking at the complex numbers or a specific field of numbers. This connection helps us count touches in the complex numbers by counting how many times they occur in a specific field of numbers, and this allows us to prove a previous conjecture about the count of touches.

This research paper proposes a novel localization approach for wireless sensor networks based on time difference and signal strength between nodes. We aim to reduce the number of required reference points by leveraging the differences in data transmission times and signal strength between adjacent nodes. A new metric called distance correlation was developed to estimate the distance between nearby nodes, and initially, three reference points were needed to determine the positions of all other nodes within the network. However, our results show that with sufficient data from nearby nodes, the number of reference points can be significantly decreased to as low as one reference point. The performance of the localization algorithm was evaluated and tested under various conditions, including different numbers of nodes, data sampling rates, and signal strength variations. Our findings indicate that a relatively low sampling rate of around 6-7 times per second is sufficient for accurate results. Additionally, the proposed algorithm was found effective in minimizing the necessary reference points to the point where a single reference point can suffice in many cases, thus significantly increasing network flexibility and efficiency.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research focuses on analyzing social media posts containing code-switching between English and Hindi to better grasp the linguistic habits of multilingual communities and gather data for applications such as sentiment analysis across language boundaries. Since current social media data annotation tools are language-specific, this project introduces a novel approach to label data that includes code-switching between languages, employing the BERT neural network model and a reinforcement learning algorithm to optimize the annotation process. This approach leverages existing annotations of single-language data to transfer knowledge and adapt to the new language, streamlining the annotation of code-switching data. Experimentation with English and Hindi code-switching data demonstrated significant improvements over traditional annotation methods.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values and minimal reflectivity. Recent studies have also considered Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanocrystals as potential enhancers for hadron therapy treatments of cancer. To understand the material's electronic behavior, researchers have used theoretical simulations to analyze Ta$_2$O$_5$ based on experiments using high-energy electron microscopes. A novel protocol was developed to treat nanoscale Ta$_2$O$_5$ based on its bulk-like behavior. Additionally, researchers have used this approach to create a practical recipe for synthesizing Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanocrystals through chemical reactions in solution. A comparison between the material's calculated and measured properties using transmission electron microscopes shows a high level of agreement, with a particular focus on how Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanocrystals change when exposed to hadron energies, with features measured in the nanoscale.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media influences, but ignored a third aspect: the impact of the physical separation of Americans in geographical regions. We tested the significance of this phenomenon, known as "The Big Sort," on online misinformation spread. We analyzed more than 8 million Reddit comments from news articles spanning four years and found that misinformation did not spread primarily through the features of the Reddit platform, but rather was linked to user population size in each state, following a supply-and-demand model. Furthermore, variations in misinformation dissemination were explained by local personality traits and cultural characteristics rather than economic, social, or political conditions. In areas where residents are less diligent in nature, and cultures place little emphasis on adherence to norms, we found increased circulation of all news, including credible sources.

We introduce a groundbreaking, efficient, and user-friendly detection algorithm called HALFADO. THIS ALGORITHM IDENTIFIES AND FLAGGS ANOMALOUS OCCURRENCES IN REAL-TIME DATA STREAMS. Developed in an algorithmic research context, HALFADO capitalizes on a limited set of labeled examples and incorporates human judgment to refine its predictions. Its design addresses a significant challenge faced by machine learning models: the slow training process. In contrast, HALFADO can be trained on a small labeled dataset due to its simple architecture. As a result, it is an attractive solution for top-performing deep learning models, which typically require substantial amounts of labeled data. HALFADO ALSO BENEFITS FROM THE FACT THAT IT CAN LEARN FROM THE DATA IT PROCESSSES IN REAL-TIME. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a simulation involving the detection of cyber threats in real-time data streams. HALFADO OUTPERFORMS A NUMBER OF COMPETITORS, INCLUDING SEVERAL SEMI-SUPERVED ALGORITHMS.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from the instructor. To effectively incorporate auditory cues present during demonstrations, understanding their underlying content and purpose must be understood. This study examines audio input from humans instructing a robot using Sawyer via spoken language by analyzing three key features: speech duration, tone variation, and speech content. Evaluating these features across four dimensions, it was discovered that instructors frequently use the same vocabulary to describe specific task elements despite varying situations such as task types, audio instructions, and errors encountered during demonstrations. However, differences in speech patterns including duration and inflection are present across these conditions, showing that human speech carries significant information relevant to machine learning tasks.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with various connection patterns. We demonstrate that this algorithm is both accurate and efficient, running in O(n) time with 'n' representing the number of desired nodes. Additionally, we explore potential applications of the algorithm, illustrating its use in deriving formulas by utilizing the underlying proof of correctness.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and their corresponding Gaussian representations. A promising approach to address this difficulty is through the study of conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, specifically focusing on the universal sector of the energy-momentum tensor in this context. A key unifying framework consists of Euler-Arnold equations and their broader integro-differential generalizations, ensuring the well-posedness of state or operator complexity optimization problems. Our comprehensive investigation extends upon our prior findings in arXiv:2005.02415, delving into intricate details of employed methodologies. A notable discussion involves differential regularization strategies, solving the integro-differential equation for Fubini-Study state complexity, and further exploring the underlying geometric properties.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting and executing tests. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python. The proposed framework, named Converse, aims to streamline the creation and execution of tests for these complex systems, allowing developers to focus on identifying defects rather than navigating underlying technologies.

Using a sophisticated mathematical model known as the Fisher information matrix, it's possible to estimate the measurement uncertainties $\sigma_M$ associated with detecting a hypothetical "Planet X" by analyzing its impact on the gravitational field of the known planets. Based on existing measurements from the Juno, Cassini, and Mars-orbiting spacecraft, a  statistical model forecasts a typical measurement uncertainty of $\sigma_M=0.22M_\oplus (d_x/400\,\textrm{AU})^3.$  Under ideal conditions, a  Planet X with mass five times that of the Earth at a distance of 400 AU can be measured with a precision of $\sigma_M=0.067M_\oplus.$  Future gravitational measurements from the Galileo spacecraft in orbit around Jupiter and the ARIEL spacecraft studying the Jupiter system will significantly reduce this uncertainty to $\sigma_M=0.019M_\oplus.$  The model also estimates the effect of various noise levels from the Galileo and ARIEL spacecraft on the measurement uncertainties $\sigma_M$ which could potentially be used to prioritize future targeted gravitational measurements.

Previous studies have demonstrated that Translation Memory (TM) can enhance Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance. Unlike existing approaches which rely on bilingual corpora for TM and employ source-side similarity searches, our proposed framework leverages monolingual data and retrieves memories in a cross-lingual manner. Notably, our framework offers two significant advantages: firstly, it enables vast amounts of monolingual data to be incorporated into TM; secondly, both the memory retriever and the NMT model can be jointly optimized for translation objectives. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves substantial gains in performance and outperforms TM-augmented NMT baselines even when utilizing bilingual TM. Furthermore, our model's capacity to tap into monolingual data allows it to excel in low-resource and domain adaptation scenarios.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and Hawking points, could provide evidence for the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model. These patterns are predicted to originate from previous black hole mergers and evaporation events. We analyzed the Planck and WMAP data using a machine learning tool called HawkingNet, and identified potential anomalies in both datasets. HawkingNet is designed to recognize the remnants of black hole evaporation, and we used it to pinpoint regions of the sky that could be associated with these events. We calculated the statistical significance of the anomalies found in both datasets, and the results suggest that the anomalies are unlikely occurrences, with a p-value of 0.0001 for the Planck data and a p-value of 0.036 for the WMAP data. We propose that the most prominent feature found in the Planck data, a low-variance circle with a radius of approximately 11 degrees, could provide evidence for the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader framework. The new results are derived from an approach simplified by Struwe in his book.

To recognize new categories from minimal labeled data, few-shot learning has been rapidly evolving in recent years. However, traditional methods that rely on average operations for calculating prototypes often struggle due to the influence of outliers. This research proposes a new, effective framework that utilizes an episodic prototype generator module to create more representative prototypes from limited support data, reducing the impact of outliers and resulting in preferable models. The framework's ability is further showcased by the substantial improvement it yields over baseline models and the comparable performance it achieves to existing methods on datasets like miniImageNet, tieredImageNet, and cross-domain benchmarks (miniImageNet to CUB-200-2011).

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommender systems. Single-target and dual-target CDR approaches are often hindered by the limitations of requiring at least one well-supplied domain and over-reliance on domain-agnostic preferences, which is impractical given the ubiquitous sparsity in real-world scenarios. To address these shortcomings, we introduce a novel framework called Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR) that tackles multi-target cross-domain recommendation in multiple sparse domains. In contrast to conventional CDR methods, MSDCR considers all participating domains as equally data-poor, thereby simultaneously enhancing the recommendation performance across each domain. We devise a Multi-Domain Separation Network (MDSN) and a Gated Aspect Preference Enhancement (GAPE) module to augment a user's specific aspect preferences in each domain by transferring complementary preferences from other domains, while maintaining domain-specific uniqueness through adversarial training and dynamically determining the degree of complementarity using GAPE. Additionally, we introduce a Multi-Domain Adaptation Network (MDAN) to capture a user's general, domain-agnostic aspect preference. By integrating the domain-specific aspect preference and the domain-agnostic aspect preference, we achieve a comprehensive user representation that can be utilized for accurate recommendations across all domains. The theoretical advantages of MSDCR are supported by rigorous mathematical proofs, and our empirical evaluations on real-world datasets unequivocally demonstrate the superior performance of MSDCR compared to state-of-the-art

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a range of pre-existing implementations of exotic cone oracles to provide a viable alternative to existing IPM frameworks. The code is highly flexible and user-friendly, allowing users to easily integrate new exotic cones into the solver by leveraging the existing oracle infrastructure. The performance of Hypatia is evaluated through a diverse set of numerical experiments, showcasing its efficiency and user-friendliness. The project boasts an open-source and community-driven approach, where all sources are available on GitHub with an accompanying tutorial to help users get started.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis, especially in large-scale neuroimaging studies. However, the success of these automated quality control systems heavily relies on sophisticated machine learning algorithms that require extensive, labeled data and complex configuration. We address this challenge by developing a novel, lightweight protocol that leverages active learning to efficiently label MRI data and enhance the accuracy of the quality control system. This protocol, specifically designed for the NIBS analysis pipeline, employs an ensemble method that integrates the predictions of diverse models to isolate anomalous data. We then applied this protocol to an ensemble of four deep learning models, utilizing active learning to gradually add more reliable data to the training set. The results showed that our protocol achieved comparable performance with fully supervised training after labeling roughly half the data. This protocol offers a practical solution for the automated quality control of MRI data, as it reduces the need for extensive, labeled data and streamlines the processing pipeline.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

Intel's Optane DC Persistent Memory Module (DC PMM) has reached commercial viability as the first commercially available nonvolatile memory DIMM. It offers fast, byte-granular data access similar to DRAM, combined with power-fail safe storage. In-depth performance evaluations have shown Optane DC PMMs to excel in read-intensive workloads, reducing latency and increasing throughput. However, benchmarks have revealed that Optane DC PMMs may struggle with write-heavy applications, where data is frequently modified before a persistent storage operation is carried out. Our research extends beyond existing performance studies, delving into the intricacies of cost-optimal memory configuration for general-purpose computing workloads. This involves optimizing a combination of included memory technologies with diverse storage characteristics, such as DRAM, Optane DC PMMs, and solid-state drives, aiming to minimize total cost while meeting performance demands. Our findings using real-world machines and simulations demonstrate that integrating Optane DC PMMs into memory hierarchies can provide the best balance of costs, potentially reducing overall expenses by up to $2,500 for specific workload scenarios.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental properties of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure. Our results match previous experimental and theoretical data on the GdSn3 compound and indicate that CmSn3 and GdSn3 both adopt a type-A anti-ferromagnetic configuration and display metallic behavior. Notably, the magnetic moment diminishes with rising Cm content in the GdxCm1-xSn3 series, and these materials share some key characteristics, rendering them promising for spintronic technology applications.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group from $SU(2) \times U(1)$ to $SU(3)\times U(1)$, while assigning the three fermion families in a non-consecutive manner. For consistency, three fermion families are necessary as indicated by triangle anomaly cancellation and asymptotic freedom. In the bilepton model, novel physical phenomena are predicted to occur, including bileptons and three types of heavy quarks: ${\cal D}$, ${\cal S}$, and ${\cal T}$. Theoretical calculations suggest that Quantum Chromodynamics will result in heavy quarks bonding to each other or light quarks to form composite particles like baryons and mesons that might be detectable with a next-generation 100 TeV particle accelerator but are too heavy for the current LHC.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends this connection to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by standardizing the ordered generating sequences, which allows us to identify exchange laws for Bn. Moreover, we establish a connection between the standard ordered generating sequences, Coxeter length, and the descent set of Bn.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of galaxies. A correlation between this approach and the residual Hubble diagram values of Type Ia supernovae holds a $3.6\sigma$ significance and is consistent with dark matter effects due to galactic halos. Furthermore, we've developed an alternative method to constrain the mass of these halos, which, under a given set of assumptions, fits the predictions made by the MOND theory. These findings imply that the mass of these halos is roughly $10^{11}$ times the mass of the Sun, with a radial density profile that decreases parabolically according to $r^{-1}$ rather than $r^{-1.5}$. If applied to the current dataset, this model is sufficient to explain the anomalies in the residual Hubble diagram without the need for extra dark energy.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 

The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth explanation of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 

The necessary background on Hilbert space-based functional analysis, operator theory, and stochastic analysis has been recapitulated within the lecture notes and further relevant references are included. 

The concluding chapter covers the pathwise approach.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, thanks to their unique optical properties in the O-band region and long-lived electronic and nuclear spin lifetimes. Although research on these defect centers has so far been conducted as part of bulk silicon studies, we demonstrate the consistent creation of high T center densities within the 220nm device layer of Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) wafers, using a process that combines ion implantation and heat treatment. By developing a method to measure spin-dependent optical transitions, we found that high T center densities located near the interface can exhibit ~1 GHz levels of spectral diffusion without the need for extensive optimization of the fabrication process.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, pain-free diagnostic images. These images enable radiologists to visually assess anatomy and physiological processes within the body, ultimately facilitating early disease diagnosis and treatment. Advanced imaging capabilities, combined with sophisticated processing techniques, enable detection of hard-to-spot tumors. This assignment delves into Automated Tumor Detection by comparing conventional image processing methods, such as morphological analysis and regional growth algorithms, in order to explore their application and effectiveness.

In this research, we explore the properties of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in an innovative algebraic framework for generating functions and symbolic evaluation functions, allowing us to derive $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$. Our findings demonstrate intriguing connections with circulant matrices and Galois fields, while showcasing the potential for $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ to be applied in computationally efficient contexts.

The high activity levels of M dwarfs present a significant challenge for discovering exoplanets, as their stellar activity masks the signals from these celestial bodies. This problem requires an effective method for filtering out the stellar activity from the data sets, especially when searching for habitable Earth-like planets. To achieve this goal, we conducted an analysis on how to optimize the line lists used for least-squares deconvolution to recover the planet signals. For this purpose, we selected the radial velocity data sets for the M dwarfs GJ 176, GJ 667C, and TRAPWN-1, and employed multiple line lists with varying levels of complexity to mitigate the stellar activity. Our results showed that the most robust approach involves utilizing a small set of narrow lines that are sensitive to the stellar radial velocity, and incorporating the synthetic spectra of multiple magnetic field configurations to account for the rotational modulation. By adopting this strategy, we were able to recover the planet signals in the data sets even when the stellar activity amplitude reached 10 m/s, and significantly improved the performance of the LLD algorithm by comparing it with the conventional approach using optimal line selection. These optimized line lists can be found in the appendices, along with the LLD parameters required to recover the planet signals, and are readily applicable to any data sets involving active M dwarfs.

This research paper proposes a pair of methods for designing a flexible and efficient data collection process in Wireless Sensor Networks, ensuring high reliability and performance. Firstly, a link quality estimation algorithm is developed, enabling swift computation of link quality between nodes. Secondly, a hierarchical sector-based system is established to organize and coordinate nodes within each sector to minimize interference and improve data transmission. The effectiveness of these methods was demonstrated through a protocol, called HBCP, which was thoroughly evaluated and subjected to various stress tests to ensure its reliability and excellence.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context for recognition in varying ways.
This study categorizes object detectors into 3 groups based on context usage:
one that doesn't use context by isolating the input, another that uses partial
context by isolating part of the feature map, and one that uses full context
without isolation.
Our evaluation method assesses the effect of context for each deep detector
category systematically. A specially designed dataset is created to test the
effect of context for deep detectors. The impact of removing the background
context and foreground objects on the MS COCO is also examined.
It is shown that both two-stage and single-stage object detectors can make use
of the context due to their extensive receptive field.
Thus, selecting the best object detector for a particular application depends
on the specific context in question.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon h_i(x)$ holds for $i=1,\ldots,k$, within the bounded domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $x$ contains the origin with smooth boundary, and for a certain condition $\beta\in [0,2)$; here $m$ denotes a function that belongs to Kirchhoff type, $f_i$ behave like $e^{\beta s^2}$, and there is a function $h_i\in \left(\big(H^1_0(\Omega)\big)^*,\|\cdot\|_*\right)$. By making use of a singular Trudinger-Moser inequality for a small positive value $\varepsilon$ and variational methods, we are able to establish sufficient conditions for a multiplicity of the system's solutions given the given conditions.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube. These vectors must adhere to either the stochastic covering property (SCP) or the strong Rayleigh property (SRP). Our findings concerning SCP measures yield new subgaussian inequalities of a bounded-difference type, surpassing earlier results by Pemantle and Peres and extending analogous outcomes for matrix-valued settings as seen in recent results by the current authors. For functions under SRP, we also obtain stronger inequalities of a bounded-difference type for matrix-valued functions, with our results building upon earlier results by the current authors for scalar functions and further exploring matrix-valued cases.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, we establish theorems enabling the comparison of crystalline and \'etale cohomologies with torsion coefficients for smooth schemes $X$ over $R$.

This study explores dihadron production in deep inelastic scattering, specifically in the case where the two hadrons have opposite signs of transverse momentum. We investigate the asymmetry in azimuthal distribution, known as $\theta_R$, and find it to be negligible. However, the asymmetry in rapidity, which we call $\Delta$, is significant and follows the pattern expected from the fragmentation of quarks and gluons. This finding supports the universality of spin-dependent hadronization functions first observed in studies of dihadron production in deep inelastic scattering, specifically in situations where the two hadrons have the same signs of transverse momentum.

We've established recently, much like our work on Deformed Special Relativity, that Fock's coordinate transformation can be developed from a novel, deformed form of the Poisson brackets.  Utilizing this approach, we successfully obtained the associated momentum transformation, which preserves the four-dimensional relationship between momentum and space, p_{\mu} x^{\nu}.  With the deformed algebra in hand, we derive the first Casimir invariant in this paper.  Following first quantization, we utilize the Klein-Gordon equation to show that Fock's spacetime corresponds to the de Sitter universe, whose spacetime radius can be defined by the invariant length representing the de Sitter hypersurface.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of forms – but also incorporate additional entities, namely, types of bilinear forms and certain types of quadratic forms. Springer's exploration of the symplectic group's conjugacy classes served as a preliminary step towards a broader investigation of the symplectic group's structure.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an embedding approach, where the Wikipedia database is hierarchically divided into layered graphs to extract entity features and learn entity representations. By combining the extracted information with a lightweight ranking method, this framework effectively suggests related entities to users on Wikipedia. We evaluate our approach through both offline and real-world online tests, demonstrating that our embeddings and recommendations exhibit desirable quality and user engagement. Furthermore, this framework delivers entity recommendations in both English and non-English languages for the Yahoo! Knowledge Graph, where Wikipedia constitutes a fundamental subset.
